title: MySQL "Client programs" flaw rated 9.1
why: Oracle rates it 9.1 but says nothing about how it works, no public MySQL release fixes it yet, there's no exploit or reported attack, it isn't on CISA KEV, and the buzz is aggregators and one vendor blog. We can't yet say who is exposed, so a page would be guesswork either way.
page_if: a fixed community release (8.4.13.1, 9.7.4.1 or a 26.10 update) ships
Oracle, the researcher or a distro explains the attack path (for example, a client connecting to a rogue server)
real exploit code or reported attacks, or a CISA KEV listing
news or researcher coverage beyond aggregators

facts.text: Oracle's November 2026 Critical Security Patch Update (17 Nov) lists 10 MySQL fixes. CVE-2026-114952 is the only critical one in MySQL Server: component "Client programs", MySQL Protocol, no login needed, CVSS 9.1 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N, confidentiality and integrity high, availability none). The 9.1 is Oracle's own score.

Affected per Oracle: MySQL Server 8.4.0-8.4.13, 9.7.0-9.7.4 and 26.10; MySQL Cluster 8.0.0-8.0.50, 8.4.0-8.4.13, 9.7.0-9.7.4 and 26.10. MySQL Server 8.0 isn't listed because Oracle no longer supports or tests it, not because it was cleared.

Oracle doesn't say which program is affected, whether the client or the server is at risk, or how the attack works. 'A client connecting to a malicious server' is a guess from the component name, not something any source confirms.

No public fix yet: the newest MySQL releases (8.4.13 and 9.7.4, 20 Oct) are inside the affected ranges, and 8.4.13.1 and 9.7.4.1 are listed as 'not yet released' with no date. TuxCare says the fix is only available to Oracle support customers.

Distros disagree on severity: Red Hat rates it Critical; Ubuntu rates it Medium and lists mysql-8.0, mysql-8.4 and mariadb as 'needs evaluation'; Debian lists mysql-9.7 in unstable as vulnerable with no fix.

No exploit: cve.now says a GitHub proof of concept was published, but the one repo it links is a read-only audit script that checks versions and never sends a request. CISA's SSVC entry says exploitation 'none'. Not on CISA KEV (catalog of 18 Nov).

Hype check: cve.now's '4 new CVEs' doesn't match Oracle's list (10 MySQL fixes, 7 of them in Server/Cluster). We couldn't find the X post claiming the 'entire LAMP stack was wiped out in 72 hours', and no source links this CVE to attacks on LAMP servers.
Unverified: whether MariaDB or Percona Server are affected. Neither has published anything on this CVE as of 20 Nov.
